title: Weekly Markets Monitor - Danger zone
gist: A weekly market wrap whose one real edge is a borrowed BCA Research framework: it is the change in the 10-year US real (TIPS) yield, not the level of nominal yields, that triggers equity drawdowns, and a ~75bp rise from the cyclical low — the trigger before 2018, 2022 and early 2025 — is nearly reached as of 21 August 2026. The surrounding week featured an expired US-Iran ceasefire, a surprise US Treasury bond-buyback increase, and a risk-off mix of falling equities, rising yields, rallying oil and a weaker dollar. Notably, despite the World Gold Council byline, the accessible text contains no gold price or gold demand analysis at all — the substance sits behind a downloadable PDF.

insights.claim: BCA Research's Dhaval Joshi finds that a roughly 75bp rise in the 10-year US real yield from a cyclical low preceded the equity market setbacks of 2018, 2022 and early 2025, making that move — not the absolute yield level — the operative equity trigger.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Gives a monitorable, falsifiable equity risk trigger: track the 10-year TIPS yield versus its cyclical low and treat ~+75bp as the drawdown alarm rather than watching nominal 10-year levels.
insights.quote: a rise in the 10-year real yield of around 75bps from a cyclical low preceded the equity market setbacks of 2018, 2022 and early 2025
insights.locator: Highlights — 'While investors focus on the level of nominal bond yields'

insights.claim: As of 21 August 2026 the 10-year US real yield sits near the ~75bp-from-the-low threshold that historically preceded equity setbacks, which is the basis for the report's 'Danger zone' framing.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Argues equity downside risk is live now, not hypothetical — a case for trimming beta or buying convexity while the threshold is being tested.

insights.claim: The report explicitly separates the two yield channels: nominal yields are high enough to force policy intervention, while the change in real yields is what transmits to equities.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Implies policymakers can cap nominal yields without removing the equity risk — a nominal-yield rescue that fails to compress real yields would leave the equity trigger armed.
insights.quote: While investors focus on the level of nominal bond yields, and they are high enough to warrant policy intervention as we saw last week, the change in real yields might matter more for equities.
insights.locator: Highlights — 'While investors focus on the level'

insights.claim: The chart's methodology footnote specifies the yield change is measured on 10-year US TIPS rather than a 9y1y forward construction, a definitional choice that changes where the 75bp threshold actually sits.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Anyone replicating the signal must use spot 10-year TIPS, not forward real rates, or the trigger level will be wrong.
insights.locator: Chart of the week: Danger zone — '*Data as of 21 August 2026'

insights.claim: The expiry of the US-Iran ceasefire, accompanied by threats of both economic and military retaliation, was a primary driver of the week's market moves.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: A live Middle East escalation path is the cleanest explanation for the oil rally and supports carrying geopolitical hedges (energy, gold, oil calls) into the ceasefire's aftermath.
insights.quote: The expiry of the US-Iran ceasefire and threats of economic and military retaliation heightened geopolitical uncertainty
insights.locator: Highlights — 'Last week, markets were driven by geopolitical tensions'

insights.claim: The US Treasury made a surprise announcement increasing bond buybacks, and this policy shock added to market volatility rather than calming it.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Signals officials view the long end as disorderly enough to intervene; unscheduled buyback changes are becoming a repeatable volatility event to position around at each refunding.
insights.quote: the US Treasury's surprise announcement of bond buyback increases added to volatility
insights.locator: Highlights — 'while the US Treasury's surprise announcement'

insights.claim: The US economy is splitting internally, with services holding strong while manufacturing and housing weaken — a composition that keeps headline growth up but concentrates the downturn in rate-sensitive sectors.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Argues against a clean recession trade; favours relative-value shorts in housing/manufacturing-levered names over an outright index short.
insights.quote: US services remained strong amid manufacturing and housing weakness

insights.claim: Europe's manufacturing recovery is broadening beyond a narrow set of countries or sub-sectors, the opposite of the US pattern where manufacturing is the weak link.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Supports a long European industrials / cyclicals versus US manufacturing exposure pair as the regional growth gap narrows.

insights.claim: China's weakness is broad-based rather than sector-specific and is severe enough to have prompted plans for fiscal stimulus.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Sets up a stimulus-announcement catalyst for China-levered commodities and equities; the weaker the data prints, the larger the fiscal response to trade.
insights.quote: China showed broad-based weakness, prompting plans for fiscal stimulus

insights.claim: Japan combined slower GDP growth with strong exports and firmer inflation, a mix that keeps the tightening case alive despite the growth miss.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Firming inflation with resilient exports argues against a dovish BoJ pivot on the GDP miss alone — relevant to JGB yields and yen carry positioning.
insights.quote: Japan saw slower GDP growth but strong exports and firmer inflation

insights.claim: India's services sector regained momentum, leaving it as one of the few major economies with an improving domestic demand pulse in the week's data.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Reinforces India as the relative-growth long within EM while China deteriorates and needs stimulus to stabilise.

themes.theme: Cross-asset price action and its internal tension

insights.claim: The week produced a specific four-way combination — equities down, bond yields up, oil up, dollar down — that is inconsistent with a pure growth scare and points instead to a supply/geopolitical shock layered on a term-premium problem.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Bonds failing to hedge equities while the dollar also weakens breaks the classic risk-off playbook and pushes hedging demand toward oil, commodities and gold instead of Treasuries.
insights.quote: Equities fell, bond yields rose, oil rallied, and the dollar weakened.

insights.claim: Despite being published by the World Gold Council under a gold and central bank demand remit, the accessible commentary contains no gold price, flow or central bank demand analysis — the gold-specific content is gated behind a 2.41mb downloadable PDF.
insights.speaker: World Gold Council
insights.so_what: Readers relying on the web version get a generic macro wrap; the actionable gold data requires the PDF, so treat the free page as a pointer rather than a source.
